end.summary:
Practised plant-eaters, meat-eaters, and animals that eat both.
Built and read food chains using arrows.
Correctly identified grass → deer and mango leaf → caterpillar links.
Correctly predicted effects when a living thing is removed from a chain.
Explained that earthworms help break down leaves; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Manav practised naming animal foods and building food chains with arrows. They successfully read the chains and predicted what could happen when one part was removed, using ideas such as fish having fewer food sources. There was some uncertainty about identifying plants and animals in a chain, but Manav later correctly identified grass as a plant and explained the caterpillar–leaf link. At home, ask them to draw one three-part food chain and explain what changes if the middle part is removed.
